topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture and outlines its focus on the initiation and resolution of inflammation.

topics.label: Innate Immune Sensing: PAMPs, DAMPs, and Discrimination Principles
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the fundamental principles by which the innate immune system senses microbial presence and tissue injury through conserved molecular patterns while distinguishing self from non-self.

topics.label: Pattern Recognition Receptors and Signaling Pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the genomic hardwiring, cellular localization, and downstream signaling cascades of pattern recognition receptors, including Toll-like receptors and the inflammasome.

topics.label: Inflammatory Execution: Sentinel Activation, Leukocyte Extravasation, and Systemic Effects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace the cellular execution of acute inflammation from sentinel mediator release and leukocyte recruitment to adaptive priming and systemic shock.

topics.label: Resolution of Inflammation, Tissue Repair, and Chronic Containment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the mechanisms that terminate acute inflammation, orchestrate tissue repair, and manage unresolved infections through granuloma formation.

topics.label: Lecture Closing
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture and previews the upcoming session on the complement system.
